entities.name: Interstitial lung disease
observations: The direct paired study evaluated 27 human patients with interstitial lung disease; the available abstract did not specify ILD subtype.
CT abnormalities were assessed by thin-section CT visual scoring and automated lung-volume analysis.

entities.name: PMID:27501892
observations: In 27 patients with ILD, phase-contrast MRI pulmonary blood flow correlated positively with CT-derived lung volume: both lungs r=0.52, p=0.006; left r=0.61, p=0.001; right r=0.54, p=0.004.
Pulmonary blood flow correlated inversely with CT visual abnormal/fibrotic area: both lungs r=-0.39, p=0.04; left r=-0.48, p=0.01; right r=-0.38, p=0.04.
After adjustment for age, height, and weight, flow-volume correlations remained positive and flow-abnormal-area correlations remained inverse and significant.

entities.name: PMID:21927998
observations: In 11 patients with pulmonary fibrosis and 11 controls, phase-contrast MRI pulmonary arterial flow was inversely correlated with CT visual score (r=-0.60, p=0.031).
The study did not report paired CT-derived lung volume.

entities.name: Flow-volume correlation
observations: In ILD, lower phase-contrast MRI pulmonary blood flow was associated with lower CT-derived lung volume; adjusted correlations remained significant.

entities.name: Flow-fibrosis correlation
observations: In ILD, lower phase-contrast MRI pulmonary blood flow was associated with greater CT visual abnormal/fibrotic lung area; adjusted partial correlations remained inverse and significant.
